newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, yield curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, yield curve flattens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Tuesday, with long bonds firming and short-term issues weaker, as investors await the conclusion of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate setting committee, analysts said.

"There was buying of the long end," said a trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "We have the FOMC results tomorrow, so I don't think anyone is fully pricing in a (rate) hike, but it would be great protection to have a bit of a flattener (trade) on or at least take off some steepness," he said.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.38 to C$110.28 to yield 7.128 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 12/32 to yield 6.71 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 42 basis points from 43 basis points at Monday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. bond investors are focused intently on the FOMC meeting which began today and ends on Wednesday. Dealers said U.S. economic data releasted last week suggested that inflation remains subdued. The data contributed to widespread expectations that the Fed will not hike interest rates during this meeting. After the FOMC meeting, traders said the next major event for the markets will be Canadian and U.S. employment data to be released on Friday.
In Canada, traders are also looking ahead to Thursday's release of details of the Government of Canada's 10-year bond auction on February 22.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.14 to C$103.95 to yield 6.449 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to two basis points from three basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.87 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.14 percent.
